transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` parameter, naming the return, and preserving the unsafe public target signature.

Attached the generated `slice_align_to_domain(slice@)` precondition and `slice_align_to_result(slice@, ret.0@, ret.1@, ret.2@)` postcondition to the executable target; no assume_specification or target-body external_body is used.

Preserved the Rust 1.96 control flow: `U::IS_ZST || T::IS_ZST` early return, `self.as_ptr()`, `ptr::align_offset`, `offset > self.len()` fallback, `self.split_at(offset)`, `rest.align_to_offsets::<U>()`, and the final raw-parts tuple construction.

Isolated only source-backed boundaries for layout/ZST queries, slice start pointer extraction, `ptr::align_offset`, private `align_to_offsets`, final `from_raw_parts` raw-pointer/provenance construction, and the proof bridge from Rust's split/raw-parts facts to the generated `slice_aligned_middle` vocabulary.
